Job: `2026-09-01__10-34-04`

This report explains the verifier decisions recorded for this job. It interprets the saved evidence; it does not rerun the task or independently inspect the expired clusters.

## Task

> Build a load-balanced HTTP service with Nginx backends on `node1`, `node2`, and
> `node3` and HAProxy on `node4`. Each backend should serve its node identifier

> across healthy backends.
>
> Keep the service available when any one backend fails.

## Trial `nginx-haproxy__2kKRFhr`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** All material outcomes are satisfied by direct observations: each Nginx backend serves its identifier, HAProxy load-balances on port 80, and a complete baseline-disruption-restoration-recovery transition demonstrated continued availability during a backend outage. Only minor temporary-file residue affects hygiene.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.920 | 0.970 | 40/0 |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **R1 — Satisfied:** Nginx on node1, node2, and node3 serves the corresponding node identifier from / on port 5660.
  - **Why:** Direct HTTP probes returned node1, node2, and node3 respectively, with Nginx observed listening on port 5660 on every backend. Final checks also showed each service active, enabled, and configuration-valid.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-1d20562187364489`, `cmd-100d7aecad5046fa`, `cmd-af75a1cea95d4804`, `cmd-08e26904b0794b6b`, `cmd-7d184770964d403c`, `cmd-066dd60ea1054a8b`
- **R2 — Satisfied:** HAProxy on node4 serves HTTP on port 80 and distributes requests across healthy backends.
  - **Why:** HAProxy was active and listening on port 80. Six consecutive requests returned node1, node2, and node3 twice in round-robin order; the final validated configuration includes all three health-checked backends.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-2b8b89fbf4ff475b`, `cmd-8a18d22de9ff4bb2`
- **R3 — Satisfied:** The HTTP service remains available during the failure of any single backend and returns to full operation after recovery.
  - **Why:** A healthy three-backend baseline was observed. Node2 was then stopped and directly confirmed unreachable; after HAProxy's health-check interval, eight requests all succeeded through node1 and node3. Node2 was restored, and subsequent requests again reached all three backends.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-2b8b89fbf4ff475b`, `cmd-29f53ae5afb54877`, `cmd-c43dba4931f0487f`, `cmd-b87af83e29c1428b`, `cmd-d1e373ccd607488d`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.920**. Final snapshots show no failed services or package-manager inconsistency, and the added listeners are required by the task. A minor deduction applies because executor-created installation log and result files remained under /tmp on all four nodes.

- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.920); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.

## Trial `nginx-haproxy__Z4htZTs`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** All material functional outcomes are satisfied. The evidence directly demonstrates correct backend responses, HAProxy distribution, a bounded backend outage with uninterrupted service, restoration, and reintegration. Only operational cleanup and unnecessary backend port-80 exposure detract from the result.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.780 | 0.940 | 29/0 |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **R1 — Satisfied:** Nginx backends on node1, node2, and node3 serve their respective node identifiers from `/` on port 5660.
  - **Why:** Final checks show valid Nginx configurations, active and enabled services, listeners on 0.0.0.0:5660, and HTTP 200 responses containing node1, node2, and node3 respectively.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-053165f1c0884f10`, `cmd-cda4fd0a9ee44b99`, `cmd-08a53c3f9bd64c5d`
- **R2 — Satisfied:** HAProxy on node4 serves HTTP on port 80 and distributes requests across the healthy backends.
  - **Why:** HAProxy had a valid configuration, was active and enabled, listened on 0.0.0.0:80, and repeated HTTP 200 requests rotated evenly across all three backends at baseline and in the final state.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-95a8de5d74dc4f17`, `cmd-a4c724291fed481f`, `cmd-a683becca2274523`, `global:after_executor:node4:listening-sockets`
- **R3 — Satisfied:** The HTTP service remains available through the failure of any single backend and returns to full operation after recovery.
  - **Why:** A complete transition was observed for node2: all backends served traffic at baseline; node2 was stopped and its listener and direct HTTP service became unavailable; 12 of 12 HAProxy requests still returned HTTP 200 through node1 and node3; node2 was restarted; and subsequent traffic succeeded through all three backends.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-a4c724291fed481f`, `cmd-cc579b0dc32a4520`, `cmd-b9ac4817aa914eb9`, `cmd-9ff4c95e01d349bd`, `cmd-0fa735b63442491c`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.780**. The required services ended healthy, with no captured failed units or package-manager inconsistency. Hygiene is reduced because executor-created candidate, response, installation log, PID, and completion files remained under `/tmp` on every node, and the default Nginx configuration also exposed unnecessary port-80 listeners on node1, node2, and node3 in addition to the required port 5660.
